one_star_reviews.text: I want to preface this review by saying that the instructors at this location are fantastic and amazing with kids and my children have absolutely loved their time with them. Unfortunately, that is where the good news ends. The owner of this location intended to close down for one week at the end of August from August 21st through August 31st to relocate to a new location and reopen on September 1st.  On August 30th, the owner sent an email out to families that the building was not ready as expected and that families would not lose the value of the classes missed and they would not be giving us an expected opening date to avoid future disappointment. On September 5th I had made a payment for my daughter and son for a month of classes. September 6th they sent out another email stating that there was no set date of reopening still, and that they would be pausing payments. I sent an email stating that I am so sorry that they are going through all of this, but that I had just paid the day prior and would like a refund. The response I got was simply that once they reopen, I would not be charged for another 30 days after. This was not what I wanted, as I would have loved to have put my kids in a different activity in the meantime with the money I spent on something that was still up in the air. But regardless, I gave them the benefit of the doubt and waited. On September 21st, after waiting for two weeks since my prior email, I sent another email stating that I would like an update and if they are not opening again soon that I would like a refund. This email was initially ignored. Two days later I reached out to one of the instructors and she apologized and said she would pass on the message that parents were looking for answers, as she had none to give (again, these instructors are amazing and this in no way reflects them). I then waited another week and on September 28th sent another email, this time saying that I have sent several emails requesting a refund for the services not rendered and I would like my money back immediately. I did not receive a response until two days later on September 30th with an apology that he had been in Belgium and was on his way back to Canada and would be contacting his lawyers and putting all blame onto the building owner and that he would hopefully have more information on Thursday. My request for a refund was ignored. I then waited until this Saturday, giving the benefit of the doubt once again even though it has now been over a month in limbo with this business keeping my money with no clear answer of when these services and obligations would be fulfilled. At this point, we have lost faith and trust that this situation is being handled in a trustworthy manner and I sent another email stating exactly that, and that if I did not receive the refund as requested several times, I would now be considering this theft. I then receive a response claiming that accusations are unwarranted and inaccurate and that he will "not accept accusation of dishonesty over circumstances beyond my control". He stated I would receive my refund, but that my "family's membership with Yamaji Dojo will be permanently terminated. Future registration or reinstatement at any of our locations will not be permitted." I find this wildly inappropriate for a business owner. There was almost no transparency throughout this entire process, my money was being held for services not being granted and after over a month of patience, the moment I state the bitter truth that taking my money and not offering the services advertised is stealing, I am the one who is at fault and shamed. My son got boxing gloves for this birthday from his grandmother and now he will not be able to use them. My kids are disappointed. There was no personal accountability taken over this matter and no attempts to make it right. Had he have just given my money back and let me know when they were back in business, we would not be in this situation at all. As of right now, I am still awaiting my promised refund.

Manager/owner got overly aggressive about a too good to go order and the value for what was paid through too good to go was insufficient
Order type

I’m writing this review because what happened to my sister at this establishment was deeply disturbing, and my own attempt to address it only made the situation more concerning.

My sister went in for a Too Good To Go order and was treated extremely disrespectfully after calmly asking a question about the advertised value of her order. The manager became aggressive, pulled the box away from her, told her to cancel the order, and repeatedly referred to her as “you people.” When my sister asked who she meant by “you people,” the comment was changed to “you,” and the manager later yelled that she was “tired of you people acting like this.”

My sister is a very calm individual, she deals with children all day so knows how to deal with emotional problems. This was also her first time at this establishment.

I was so disturbed by what I heard that I called the business myself and asked to speak with Sahday, who we were told was the owner. The female employee who answered told me, “I don’t know when she’s gonna be in,” and then hung up on me.

That is an absolutely unacceptable way to handle a serious customer complaint.

If the owner or management genuinely believes that nothing inappropriate happened, why not have a conversation with the customer? Why simply hang up?

What makes this even more disappointing is the apparent approach to negative reviews. Instead of acknowledging customers' concerns and attempting to resolve them, the responses seem focused on disputing customers' accounts and shifting blame back onto them. That is not accountability.

And before anyone tries to turn this into an argument about a Too Good To Go order: the issue is not the pizza. The issue is how a customer was spoken to and treated when she calmly asked a question.

The repeated “you people” comments were completely unnecessary and, given the context, were perceived as discriminatory. Being treated this way by a business is unacceptable regardless of what the original disagreement was about.

I have always liked the small-business culture in Georgetown and genuinely want to support local businesses. But supporting local businesses should not mean overlooking disrespectful or discriminatory treatment.

This is not the Georgetown I want to support.

And regarding the business's responses to these reviews: if the accounts being described are supposedly false or inaccurate, there is a straightforward way to establish what actually happened:  review the security footage. If there is footage that contradicts these accounts, let it speak for itself. This business has been gaslighting through responses to negative comments to mislead people.

I am not going to claim that other reviews are fake or purchased because I cannot independently prove that. But after seeing how complaints are being handled, I can say that I personally question the credibility of the overall review picture.

Customers deserve to be treated with basic dignity and respect. A business should not become defensive, aggressive, or dismissive simply because someone asks a reasonable question.

I will not be supporting this establishment, and I hope others think carefully about the way this business treats its customers before deciding where to spend their money.
Order type
Take out

1 star — Extremely disrespectful experience

I have never experienced this level of disrespect from a business, especially over something as simple as asking a question about an order.

I placed a Too Good To Go order that was advertised on the app as an $18 value for pizza. When I arrived, the employee handed me a basic pepperoni medium pizza. I politely asked because the app stated that the order was supposed to have an $18 value.

Out of nowhere, the manager cut the employee off and said, “This is what we are supposed to do.” She then started pulling the pizza box back across the table and told me to cancel the order. Before I had even had an opportunity to decide what I wanted to do, she said, “Okay, you're going to cancel the order.”

I calmly asked why she was being aggressive and pulling the box away when I hadn't even touched it. Her response was:

“You people like to order and take the box and cancel after.”

I asked her, “Who is ‘you people’?” I was literally the only customer in the store, and this was my first time ordering from this business. She then clarified with “you.”

She proceeded to pack up to leave for her next delivery and, while leaving, yelled:

“I’m tired of you people acting like this.”

I want to be very clear: I remained calm and respectful throughout this entire interaction. I did not yell, threaten, insult, or behave aggressively toward anyone. I was simply asking a reasonable question about an order.

The repeated use of “you people” was completely unnecessary and, in the context of the interaction, was deeply offensive and discriminatory. I was shocked by the way I was spoken to and treated as a customer.

After this, I employee said that she is the manager and owner. She called the employee from the road, and after the call, the staff stopped communicating with me. I asked the staff who the other owner was, and they refused to tell me.

one_star_reviews.text: Almost always don't have bread ready, on Sunday they say open at 9am, but it's actually 9:30 because they don't show up till 9 am. Also, if you like listening to a conversation in Hindi while watching your sub get cold, this is the subway for you. Do better, this is ridiculous

I really don’t like leaving negative reviews, but I feel this experience is worth bringing to the attention of both management and other customers.

Unfortunately, this isn’t the first time I’ve noticed a decline in quality at Subway. Over the past few years, I’ve found that many locations have become increasingly inconsistent, particularly when it comes to portion sizes and making orders correctly. At this point, I’m seriously questioning whether I’ll continue going to Subway.

I placed an order this afternoon for two footlong sandwiches for pickup. I was honestly shocked by how light they felt. Both sandwiches were missing two of the ingredients I ordered. Also, two ingredients should have had „extra“ (as I’ve noticed the trend of continuous sandwich shrinkage) and one them were missing altogether.

As you can see from the photos, there is also very little lettuce, and there are several inches of bread with virtually no filling. The sandwiches were unusually hollow and sparse. In the past, Subway sandwiches were packed enough that keeping the ingredients inside the bread could actually be a challenge. They were filling and felt like a reasonable value. This was very different. I still felt hungry after a footlong.

I understand that portion sizes can vary somewhat, and I certainly don’t expect employees to pile ingredients onto a sandwich. But there is a significant difference between a reasonable portion and receiving substantially less than what was ordered—especially when ingredients are missing entirely.

I hope management takes this seriously. Whether this is an issue with individual employees, store management, training, or simply trying to reduce food costs, the long-term result is the same: customers notice. If people consistently feel they are paying full price for less and less food, eventually they will simply stop coming.

I’m not posting this because I want to attack anyone. I’m posting it because I actually remember when Subway sandwiches were much more consistent and filling, and I would rather see the company address the problem than continue leaving customers feeling short changed. Some people work a whole hour just to pay for their lunch or dinner there.

Unfortunately, after this experience, I think I may have reached my limit with Subway.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, this was an extremely disappointing introduction to professional karting for our family.

My 7-year-old son absolutely loves karting and has been driving since he was very young, but we are completely new to the professional racing world. I reached out to this facility specifically because I wanted someone experienced to assess him, see where he was at, and guide us on what the best next step would be.

From the beginning, I felt like I was bothering one of the owners simply by asking questions. His emails were short, dismissive and often came across as annoyed — despite knowing that I was a parent who was brand new to this and looking to them for guidance.

We arranged a session, and at NO point beforehand was I clearly told that this one session would cost $425. Had I been told that upfront, I would not have agreed to it.

When I questioned the charge afterward, rather than acknowledging that a $425 fee should have been clearly communicated before the session, I was told that I should have asked about the price.

That response really bothered me. When someone comes to your business specifically saying they are new to the sport and asking for your expertise, part of good customer service should be explaining what you’re recommending AND what it will cost before proceeding — not expecting a brand-new customer to know which questions they should be asking.

After I raised the issue, the owner told me he would refund $175 and asked me for my email address so he could send it that day. I provided it. The refund was never sent.

That honestly made an already disappointing experience even worse. If you tell a customer you are issuing a refund to resolve a situation, then follow through on what you said you would do.

If you’re new to professional karting and considering this facility, GET ALL PRICING IN WRITING before you show up. Ask exactly what you are being charged for, what is included and what the total will be. And if you’re promised a refund or adjustment, I would recommend getting that confirmed in writing as well.

Beyond the pricing, the overall vibe was simply not welcoming. As a parent trying to introduce an excited 7-year-old to a sport he absolutely loves, I expected guidance, enthusiasm and a facility that made a new family feel welcome. Instead, I repeatedly felt like we were bothering them by being new and asking questions.

For an industry that should want to encourage the next generation of young drivers, that was probably the most disappointing part of the entire experience.

We absolutely will not be returning.

Very disappointing experience — I would not recommend this workshop for beginners.

I enrolled in the Modelling Workshop as a complete beginner with absolutely no previous modelling experience. I signed up expecting to actually be taught modelling through structured, practical instruction.

Unfortunately, after attending the first two classes, I did not feel that I was actually being taught the skills I enrolled to learn.

The first class mainly involved someone from an agency coming in and explaining who they were, what they do and how their agency operates. I understand that this information may be useful, but it was not modelling training, and I did not feel I learned any actual modelling skills from that class.

The second class focused on posing and posture. My experience was that we were largely told to try different things ourselves rather than being properly taught how to pose. As a complete beginner, I expected the instructor to demonstrate the techniques, explain what to do, physically/directly guide the positioning, identify what I was doing incorrectly and teach me how to improve.

That was the biggest disappointment for me: I enrolled to learn modelling, but I did not feel that the actual modelling techniques were being taught.

After only two classes, I felt that I had gained very little practical knowledge and, instead of building confidence, the experience left me discouraged and questioning whether I could even do modelling.

I raised my concerns directly with TFA. They initially told me there would be no refund under the agreement. They later offered me a $303.70 pro-rata refund from the $1,334.82 I had paid and offered to move the remaining classes to a one-on-one male instructor. I respectfully declined because, after my experience, I no longer felt comfortable continuing the workshop.

I am sharing this review because I believe prospective students — especially complete beginners — should know about my experience before spending this amount of money.

This is my personal experience and opinion based on the two classes I attended and my communications with TFA.

one_star_reviews.text:
The food used to be really good, which is why I’ve come back before, but lately, the quality doesn’t seem to be what it used to be. And unfortunately, the attitude of the cashier left a very poor impression.

The last time I ordered the 9B, there was barely any shrimp, and there was virtually no shredded chicken to speak of. The filling was mostly egg and bean sprouts, with hardly any actual meat.

I also want to be fair about the price. At around $15, we understand that we cannot expect a large amount of shrimp, chicken, or other more expensive ingredients. We are not asking for an unreasonable amount of meat or seafood. What we are asking for is simply a portion that is reasonably consistent with what is actually described on the menu. If shrimp and shredded chicken are listed as ingredients, customers should reasonably be able to see and taste them. Finding half a shrimp or such a small amount of shredded chicken that it is practically impossible to find among the egg and bean sprouts is simply disappointing.

Because of that previous experience, when I ordered the same 9B again this time, I parked outside and asked my brother to go in and pick it up for me. I specifically reminded him to politely ask the staff to make sure the portion was complete, simply because of what had happened with our previous order.

When my brother received the 9B, he opened the box and checked it before leaving the restaurant to make sure everything was there. This was not done to be difficult or demanding. It was simply a reasonable precaution to avoid having to come back later if something was missing or the order was not prepared as expected.

While he was checking the food, the cashier repeatedly gave him very obvious dirty unfriendly looks and visibly showed annoyance toward him. This was particularly uncomfortable because my brother was not being rude, demanding, or disrespectful in any way. He was simply checking an order that we had just paid for.

We were paying for our food, not asking for a handout. We were not treating anyone as though they were beneath us, nor were we trying to tell anyone how to do their job. We simply wanted to make sure we received what we paid for, especially after having an issue with the exact same item before. Our request was made politely and respectfully.

A cashier is one of the first points of contact between a customer and a business, so their attitude naturally becomes part of the customer’s impression of the entire restaurant. If you value the business you work for and the hard work that the owner and the rest of the team put into running it, professionalism should also be reflected in how customers are treated.

I hope the owner can take this feedback constructively. We understand the price point, and we are not expecting a $15 dish to be loaded with meat or seafood. We simply expect the food to reasonably match the description on the menu, and we expect customers to be treated with basic courtesy when they politely raise a concern or check their order.

A customer checking their food before leaving should not be made to feel uncomfortable for doing something completely reasonable. Food portions can always be improved, but a respectful and professional interaction costs nothing and can make a significant difference to the overall customer experience.

Thanks!

Avoid this lounge. Extremely disappointing experience and absolutely not worth the money.
I used the Plaza Premium Lounge in Terminal 3 US Transborder today. The receptionist was excellent — friendly, professional, and she warned me that it was very busy. Unfortunately, everything after that was horrible.
The lounge was overcrowded, noisy, and poorly managed. People were using extra seats and tables for bags and luggage while other guests had nowhere to sit. Staff did not seem to manage this at all, so customers had to ask other people themselves to move their belongings just to get a chair or somewhere to put a cup.
Other than the receptionist, I found the staff unwelcoming and impolite. The atmosphere did not feel relaxing or “premium” in any way.
The food was also very poor. The oatmeal was extremely watery, the sausages were dry, the omelette looked like it had been sitting there for a long time, and the selection was very limited. There was a muffin drawer but no muffins, and it was not replenished. Even the coffee machine had only a handful of choices. There was also nobody available to serve alcohol while I was there.
Even clearing dishes was poorly organized — there was nowhere convenient to leave your plate, so at one point I basically had to hold it until someone came to collect it.
For roughly US$32–$55, or even using a complimentary lounge entitlement, this is terrible value.
My advice: skip this lounge and go to one of the regular restaurants or Starbucks in the terminal instead. For $20–$30 you can get decent food, a proper seat and table, more space, and probably a much more pleasant environment.
Other airport lounges may be worth paying for, but this particular lounge is not. Avoid it.

She eventually removed the lenses and told me that her boss would have to put them into the new frames because she was unable to do it herself.

When I picked up my glasses, I unfortunately could not properly test them before leaving because I had contacts in. Once I got home, removed my contacts and put the glasses on, I immediately noticed that my lenses were completely scratched and cloudy. I could barely see through them. These are also transition lenses, so they change into sunglasses in the sun.

I called the optical immediately to explain what had happened. During that conversation, the lady told me to call welfare and tell them that I could not see out of my prescription and that I needed a new eye examination so that I could get new glasses. I told her that I was not comfortable doing that because it would not be truthful. I had my eyes examined and these glasses made in April 2025, and I had brought them to the store because the arm was broken — not because there was anything wrong with my lenses.

When I questioned the damage to my lenses, she became upset, repeatedly said that she would hang up if I continued to blame the store, and ultimately hung up the phone.

I was left with damaged glasses that I could no longer use and had to find another optical to replace them. Thankfully, my OW worker was able to help me with the situation, or I would have been screwed.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am beyond frustrated and disgusted with my experience at Pizzaville. What should have been a simple pizza delivery turned into an absolutely ridiculous and unnecessarily stressful situation, all because of the restaurant's poor communication, lack of professionalism, and refusal to take responsibility for its own mistakes.

I placed an order through Uber Eats and selected "Leave at Front Door" as my delivery preference. This restaurant does not use uber drivers to deliver their food, but instead they use their own. No problem. Despite this, the restaurant failed to properly update the delivery status. My order remained stuck on "Prepping for Delivery" and was NEVER updated to "Heading Your Way" or marked as delivered.

How exactly is a customer supposed to know their food has arrived when the restaurant doesn't bother updating the order status or notifying them?

Because of this complete failure in communication, my pizza was left sitting outside for an unknown amount of time. By the time I discovered it, there were bugs in my food. Absolutely disgusting and completely unacceptable. I paid for freshly prepared food to be delivered to my home, not for pizza to be left outside collecting bugs because the restaurant couldn't manage something as basic as delivery notifications.

What made this experience even worse was the restaurant's attitude when I called to explain what happened. Instead of apologizing or acknowledging that their failure to update the delivery status contributed to the problem, the staff were extremely argumentative and defensive. It felt like they were more interested in arguing with me than resolving a legitimate customer complaint.

After all that unnecessary back and forth, the owner finally agreed to prepare and send a replacement pizza. However, this meant my food arrived approximately 1 hour later than the original expected delivery time. An entire hour of additional waiting because of a situation that could have been completely avoided.

But somehow, the experience managed to get even worse.

When the replacement pizza finally arrived, THE DELIVERY DRIVER REFUSED TO GIVE ME MY FOOD UNTIL I HANDED OVER THE ORIGINAL PIZZA THAT HAD BEEN SITTING OUTSIDE WITH BUGS ON IT!

Are you serious?!

After the restaurant failed to communicate the delivery, left me with food that had bugs on it, argued with me when I complained, and made me wait an additional hour, they then had the audacity to withhold my replacement pizza until I returned the contaminated food!

The fact that I was made to feel as though I had done something wrong, when I was simply expecting the food I paid for to be delivered properly, is absolutely infuriating.

A replacement pizza should have been the bare minimum, not something I had to argue for and then negotiate with the delivery driver to receive.

What frustrates me most is the complete lack of accountability. Mistakes happen, and I understand that. But when a business makes a mistake, the appropriate response is to acknowledge it, apologize, and make things right, not argue with the customer, waste their time, and make the entire situation even more unpleasant.

I shouldn't have to constantly check my front door while an app tells me my food is still being prepared. I shouldn't have to discover bugs on food that I paid to have delivered. And I certainly shouldn't have to deal with argumentative staff and a delivery driver refusing to hand over a replacement order.

Pizzaville seriously needs to improve its delivery procedures, communication, and customer service. This was one of the most frustrating food delivery experiences I've ever had.

Absolutely unacceptable from beginning to end. I will think twice before ever ordering from this location again.

Previously deleted my low review as management finally started helping but the issues keep on stacking up and i continue to be ignored and disappointed by the company.

Management is slow to respond if they respond at all, to our complaints and issues.

The apartment is listed as AC which is true for the living room, but the cheap construction makes the bedrooms about 5-10 degrees warmer than the living room.

I don’t even know where to begin with the parking… it’s horrendous and clearly not thought out. We were the first people to move into the complex and were informed we get 1 reserved stall and 1 flex but the flex is just above ground and there will be lots. We are in building 4000 and months into our tenancy the company decided to designate specific stalls for flex and put them infront of other buildings and left none near building 4000… not to mention the parking being full already. I am paying 40 a month for a gamble in a parking stall, this isn’t even a downtown residential property lol.

We thought the amenities would be nice but we moved in before it was finished and seeing it now it’s the smallest building ever. Keep in mind there is 4 large apartments at this location plus several townhouses, once construction is complete the amenities will be unusable.

The walls are thin, continuous noise of dogs in the complex through all hours of the day and it sounds like they are in your room. The road noise is loud and the construction is unbearable. Our floor smelt like urine for several weeks and took several complaints to get addressed… luckily management was able to fix it somewhat but this basically sums up the living conditions. Going back to the cheap construction the windows appear to be super cheap and don’t insulate at all. It sounds like your window is open and you can feel the sun coming through even with black out curtains.

The construction continues to fail on the road and around the building. Since moving in around May they have had to re-do the parking lot and sidewalk as it began cracking, causing tenants to have to walk through active construction zones just to get home.

I don’t like leaving negative reviews especially because the management team on site have been super friendly but they are way too busy to address  the severity of the flaws this place has. I have given reasonable amount of time for management to work with me but the lack of response is unprofessional.

There are several other issues I won’t get into in this review. My main concern is being ignored on a breach of the tenancy act.

For the price this place charges which is insane by the way, do not even waste your time looking at these units.

one_star_reviews.text:
First and last time.
We walked in and asked for a table inside with a view because of allergies. At that point, honestly, I would have settled for a view of literally anything other than the windows. The windows looked like they hadn’t been cleaned since the invention of glass. I’m pretty sure dogs have had more interaction with them than the cleaning staff.

The tables were another adventure. Whatever they use to clean them leaves them sticky as all hell. Nothing says “welcome to dinner” quite like wondering if your forearm is going to remain permanently attached to the table.

The middle-aged woman working at the bar was… enthusiastic. Very enthusiastic. There were four people trying to have a conversation and somehow we all ended up participating in hers. She was so loud I’m fairly certain the neighbouring tables now know her entire life story.

Our server came over and spoke at approximately mouse volume, which might have been lovely under normal circumstances, but unfortunately we were competing with the speakers and the woman at the bar who apparently had a microphone installed in her throat.

Ordered two Cokes. Apparently, you have to specifically request that Coke be fresh and carbonated. Rookie mistake on our part. These came with a few decorative ice cubes floating around in them. A refreshing little surprise.
I also wasn’t thrilled that my straw arrived already sitting inside my drink. I have no idea who handled it, whether it had a wrapper at one point, or where it had been on its journey to my table. But apparently the straw had already lived a full life before meeting me.

Then came the food.

The broccoli cheddar bites were so overcooked that both my husband and I nearly needed burn treatment. 🔥

The sweet potato fries were tiny little pieces of sadness with a truly disgusting flavour.

The bison burger arrived with one piece of roasted red pepper, which had achieved a texture somewhere between mush and baby food. Then came the “micro greens”—and I mean MICRO. Enough to potentially choke on, but apparently not enough to actually taste.
And none of it was hot. At best, it was warm-ish.

Then there was the Class A Chicken Burger. I’m still trying to figure out the purpose of the panko crumbs because when they’re burnt, they apparently exist solely to add crunch and disappointment. Couldn’t taste the cheese. There was sauce… apparently?! The “smoked bacon” seemed to have skipped the smoking part and gone straight to raw. The lettuce arrived pre-wilted, and the bun had the structural integrity of a hockey puck.

At this point I have to ask: Is there seriously no other bun available in the Kawartha Lakes? 😂

By the end of the meal, we were mostly just impressed that every course managed to introduce a new problem.

We were cautioned not to go here.
We should have listened.

Still trying to figure out how this culinary experience somehow came to $83.

Needless to say, we will not be returning. The only thing fresh about this visit was our regret.

one_star_reviews.text:
DO NOT BUY FROM THE SHOPPING CHANNEL — ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE

This has been one of the worst online shopping experiences I have ever had.

We ordered a Casper mattress through The Shopping Channel (TSC) on September 6. As of today, we still had not received the mattress.

For THREE STRAIGHT WEEKS, I repeatedly contacted TSC trying to find out where our order was. Every time, I was given essentially the same excuse: “It’s a third-party seller. We’ll look into it and get back to you within two business days.”

They didn't.

No call. No email. No meaningful follow-up. Nothing.

I had to keep contacting them over and over again just to get any information about an order they had taken our money for.

When I finally demanded a full refund because the product had not been delivered, TSC initially refused. They continued claiming the mattress had shipped.

Except FedEx said otherwise.

FedEx tracking showed that a shipping label had been created — but the package had not actually been received by FedEx. Creating a shipping label is NOT the same thing as shipping a mattress.

Despite this, TSC continued to hide behind the claim that it had shipped.

I eventually had to wait until the following month before getting the refund.

The mattress never arrived. The promised callbacks never happened. The tracking didn't show that FedEx ever received the shipment. And instead of taking responsibility and fixing the problem, TSC repeatedly pushed the issue onto the third-party seller and made me chase them for weeks.

This is not customer service.

If TSC is going to sell products through third-party vendors, they should still take responsibility when customers have problems. Taking someone's money and then telling them to wait while nobody actually follows up is completely unacceptable.

My advice: avoid ordering a Casper mattress through The Shopping Channel. Based on my experience, if something goes wrong, be prepared to spend weeks chasing customer service yourself.

Very disappointing experience with both TSC and Casper, and one I will not be repeating.

I have mixed feelings about Hairy Tarantula because, for a long time, it was a place I genuinely enjoyed and looked forward to visiting every week.

I originally started attending Pokemon pre-releases there before becoming heavily involved in the One Piece TCG community. During my first year of attending One Piece locals, I had an excellent experience. I met a welcoming group of players, made lasting friendships, and always looked forward to Tuesday nights after a long day of work. Playing my Green Bonney deck, hanging out with friends, and being part of the community became one of the highlights of my week.

Unfortunately, things began to change after one of the associates who normally ran the events went on vacation and another person took over. One incident that particularly stood out involved a verbal altercation between the organizer and a friend of mine. I felt some of the comments and behavior displayed were inappropriate and unprofessional.

What made the situation even more uncomfortable was that friend was repeatedly questioned throughout the evening about his relationship with someone who had previously left a negative review of the store. From my perspective, it felt less like a conversation and more like an interrogation. He was asked about it multiple times, despite clearly not wanting to be involved, and by the end of the night he felt singled out and attacked. It created an atmosphere that was very uncomfortable for everyone present.

Around the same time, the events themselves seemed to become less organized. There were a few incidents when the organizer forgot to conduct the prize raffle, which had been a common part of local events. Many players stayed behind expecting the raffle to take place, only to be told that it would not be happening and then be asked to leave the store. It was disappointing and left many of us feeling overlooked.

Another concern is product pricing. I completely understand that every store has the right to set its own prices, and consumers ultimately decide whether they want to pay those prices. However, I often found products to be priced significantly above market. While that is certainly the store's decision, it can feel discouraging for regular attendees who consistently support the store through event participation and purchases.

I also think there is room for improvement when it comes to rewarding and supporting the local player base. Many other stores find small ways to recognize regular customers and event participants. While I understand the importance of keeping things fair and accessible, issues such as obvious botting and scalping for event registrations made many of my friends and me feel discouraged about participating in events. It often felt difficult for genuine local players to access opportunities intended for the community.

While there were certainly staff members who went above and beyond and provided excellent customer service, I rarely found the overall staff experience particularly welcoming. In my opinion, the players themselves were the primary reason the community felt as inclusive and enjoyable as it did. The friendships and connections built among the regulars were what kept many of us coming back week after week.

That is ultimately why this review is disappointing for me to write. I know firsthand how great the experience at Hairy Tarantula can be because I lived it for over a year. The community that existed there was something special, and many of the people I met became genuine friends. Unfortunately, various decisions and experiences over time have made it difficult for me to continue participating in events there.

This review is not written out of spite. I genuinely want Hairy Tarantula to succeed and improve. There is a great community there, and that community deserves an environment where players feel welcomed, valued, and respected. I hope management takes feedback like this seriously because I'd love to see the store return to the atmosphere that made it such a special place for so many of us in the first place.

We understand if this is the restaurant’s policy, but it should have been explained to us at the beginning. We certainly did not expect to finish the entire bottle in less than an hour.

I explained that the situation had not been handled properly. Both the server and the manager acknowledged that they had failed to mention the policy and agreed that they should have informed us. I had a very disappointing experience at this salon on September 25.
I called as a walk-in and made an appointment for nail refill , and I arrived about 10 minutes later. I waited around 15 minutes before the nail technician came.
As soon as she started filing my nails, I could tell that I was going to have a problem with the shape. I specifically asked for the tips to be slightly almond-shaped, not extremely pointed, just with a little bit of definition at the tip. Unfortunately, the technician ,Mojgan, clearly did not know how to create the shape I was asking for. She kept filing the sides of my nails, leaving the tips flat and uneven.
I repeatedly asked her to fix the shape, but instead of correcting it, she kept giving excuses as to why it couldn’t be done. Is it really that difficult to make the length and shape of the nails consistent? Every single nail ended up looking different.
To make matters worse, she stopped in the middle of doing my nails to work on another client. I immediately spoke to the salon manager and explained that I was in a hurry. Obviously, if I had plenty of time, I wouldn’t have booked a walk-in appointment in the first place.
The manager eventually moved me to another nail technician, and I have to say that I had no issue with the second technician. She genuinely tried to fix the situation and save my nails. However, by that point, the first technician had filed so much from the sides of my nails that there was very little left to work with. We had no choice but to cut my nails shorter so the second technician could create a somewhat decent shape.
The entire process took an unreasonable amount of time. The second technician did her best, and I appreciate her effort, but because my nails and surrounding skin are sensitive, my skin became extremely irritated and even started bleeding around several nails. This entire situation was caused by the poor work of the first technician.
What upset me even more was the lack of professionalism and accountability from the salon. When it was time to pay, the salon manager simply put a $76 payment terminal in front of me without even asking what happened or offering an apology.
I was extremely upset and asked why I should be paying full price for a service that had gone so badly. I even said that if I was going to pay anyone extra, I would rather pay the second technician for the additional time and effort she spent trying to fix the first technician’s work.
I ended up paying $65, but I did not receive a genuine apology or any acknowledgment of how badly the situation had been handled. Instead, I felt like I was being treated as though the salon had done me a favor simply by giving me an appointment.
I also want to mention that, Mojgan ,had previously done my eyebrows, and I was not satisfied with that service either.
I have never experienced this level of poor workmanship and lack of accountability at a salon. I lost a significant amount of time, had to rush through the rest of my plans, and ultimately left with irritated and bleeding skin around my nails.
I would not recommend this salon, and I personally will not be returning.👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼

Appalling Customer Service from Store Manager Nick

I recently purchased automotive touch-up paint from Canadian Tire on the recommendation of a salesman named Tyler, after explaining that I needed it for a minor scratch on my Subaru BRZ's alloy wheel.

The product came with inadequate instructions, and when I attempted to open it, black paint spilled onto my hardwood floor and white ceramic table, leaving an unsightly stain.

When I returned to the store, an employee named Brian was courteous, professional and promptly processed my refund. Unfortunately, the arrival of store manager Nick demonstrated just how quickly good customer service can deteriorate under poor management.

Rather than listening to my concerns, Nick adopted what I found to be a condescending, dismissive and defensive attitude. He suggested the product was straightforward to use and questioned how I could have made a mistake. When I challenged him to demonstrate its supposedly simple operation, he declined and suggested finding someone from the automotive department instead. No demonstration ever materialized.

He then argued that the product was intended for body scratches rather than wheels, completely missing the point that the incident occurred while OPENING the container, not applying the paint.

To make matters worse, despite Brian having already processed my refund, Nick indicated that he preferred to compensate me with Canadian Tire money rather than return my actual money.

Apparently, the product was simple enough for Nick to question a customer's competence, but not simple enough for him to demonstrate himself.

The contrast between Brian's professionalism and Nick's attitude was striking.

A manager should be setting the standard for customer service, not providing a textbook example of how to alienate customers.

Canadian Tire would do well to remind Nick that his job is to resolve customer problems, not make customers regret bringing them to his attention.

Words cannot express how much I hate this Kia location. I have been trying to get ahold of the service department now on and off for 5 weeks and they never answer the phone or return messages. I was hoping it was a hiccup during the buying process but this location doesn’t care about NEW or EXISTING customers at all

I came in to Clarington Kia on March 2nd and I spoke with Karl who started off very good with talking to me about different vehicles and what not, I found a 2023 Sorento that I really liked and he mentioned that if I wanted it I should act fast because they sell quick. It being a late Saturday night and them being closed on Sunday I figured I’d take my chances and come back on Monday with my partner to discuss the financing and show him the vehicle I decided on. Bad luck because the car ended up selling on Monday morning before I came back. Not their fault, things happen. I went back and spoke with Karl and he said that the cars are super easy to find and if I give him 3 colour choices he can have one for me by the end of the week, give him a few days, but he needed a $1000 deposit. So I paid the deposit and said that I only wanted the grey of the last one I saw and he said ok, might be a little harder but I’ll do it. (All happened around 630 Monday night) Tuesday morning before I even woke up Karl had called to tell me that there was no chance he could find the vehicle he sold me and that if I wanted that vehicle I’d have to get the 2024. So I went into the dealership and spoke with him and it turns out the 2024 with a few more specs was only 1400 more. A couple questions came to mind, 1) why wouldn’t he had offered me that to begin with, especially with such a small price difference. 2) would they maybe cover the cost because of the miscommunication on the car I purchased and 3) how would this affect timeline and my trade in value.

They did not cover the cost and Karl pretty much laughed at me saying I’ll give you your deposit back before I do that because these cars sell themselves. And that my timeline is 2-4 weeks for delivery so as long as my vehicle is in similar condition it should be the same but try not to drive a lot. Keep in mind this is March 4th. On March 7th he said he recieved the VIN. On March 20th I asked for an update as I hadn’t heard from him and he said it’s in compound and on April 7th I asked where my vehicle was and he replied he’s no longer with the company, reach out to Kia if I want an update. It is now April 17th, the dealership still has my deposit and not one person has contacted me before Karl left or after Karl left to give me any information about my vehicle. Karl only gave me information when I reached out. I’m astonished that someone left the company but didn’t bother to let clients know until they reach out to him and even more astonished that no one has reached out to me to even let me know they took over the deal. I have no idea where my car is, I have no idea where my money is and more importantly I have no contact besides a generic phone number to call.
The messiest winners I’ve ever been at. No organization at all. Can’t even walk through the isles without stepping over boxes

Misleading Advertising – Smokehouse Pulled Pork Promo

​I went in to order the limited-time Smokehouse Pulled Pork based on the promotional sign right above the counter. The main photo prominently displays the sandwich alongside a fountain drink and a bag of Lay's chips, giving customers the clear impression that the listed prices (Small $9.99, Regular $12.99, Large $15.99) are for a complete meal combo.

​However, after ordering, I found out that those prices are strictly for the sandwich alone—the drink and chips shown in the center of the ad are not included.

​Featuring items in the primary promotional image without any clear disclaimer stating "sides sold separately" or "combo upgrade required" is deceptive marketing. If a drink and chips are shown right behind the sandwich in the main product photo, customers reasonably expect that to represent what they are buying. Please update your signage to be transparent about what is actually included in the price.

I had a few recent bad experiences here. The owner responded to a previous complaint but I think my concern has been reduced to whether individual requests were technically completed, when that wasn’t the main issue.

I understand that Fresh Burrito is not a vegetarian-only restaurant, and I never expected it to be. My point about the gloves was about consideration when moving directly from handling meat to preparing a vegetarian order. I did ask for the gloves to be changed, and they were changed after I asked. Other restaurants that serve both meat and vegetarian food routinely take similar precautions, sometimes without the customer needing to request it, so I don’t think this is an unreasonable concern.

The larger issue was the employee’s attitude and the overall way the order was being prepared. He seemed rushed, dismissive and more focused on quickly putting the bowl together than listening carefully to what I was asking for. Having one request, such as extra beans, completed correctly does not mean the overall interaction was attentive.

The hot sauce is also not just about expecting a mathematically exact “three dots.” I was clearly communicating that I wanted a very small amount, because I have had the same issue at this location before where more hot sauce was added than requested. When a customer repeatedly emphasizes “only a little,” the concern is whether that preference is actually being listened to. Offering to remove it afterward does not change the experience of repeatedly having to correct the preparation while the bowl is being made.

I also said it was okay in the moment because I did not want to continue going back and forth with the employee. That should not be interpreted as meaning I was satisfied with the service.

My review was about the combination of the employee’s attitude, the rushed/sloppy preparation, and repeatedly having to advocate for fairly simple requests. I would have appreciated a response that acknowledged that aspect of the experience rather than primarily explaining why each individual action was justified.

I’m sharing this because this was not my first experience with this issue, and based on other customer feedback, concerns about service and how complaints are handled do not appear to be unique to me. I hope the feedback is taken as an opportunity to improve rather than something that needs to be disproven point by point. Judging by the other negative feedback here, there is a clear behaviour issue and poor customer service hare.
